title: Character Census

story.briefing: Every packet on this line is padded with filler. Whichever character dominates the padding identifies which relay produced it.
story.success: Relay fingerprinted. The source of the malformed packets is named.

description: Given a string, return the character that appears most often. If several characters tie for most frequent, return whichever comes first in ASCII order. For an empty string, return an empty string.

examples.explanation: Both appear once, so ASCII order decides.

hints: Counting occurrences by character is the same shape of problem as counting occurrences by number — a map from key to count.
The tie-break is what makes this fiddly. Whichever order you iterate the counts in, you must compare deliberately rather than relying on insertion order.
Build a map of character to count in one pass. Then walk the entries keeping the best: replace the current best when the count is higher, or when the count is equal and the character sorts earlier.
